AttachIntervenantRequest.description:
Validates a request to attach an intervenant to a beneficiary.

Authorisation pivots on the *beneficiary*: assigning who serves a
beneficiary is conceptually a mutation of the beneficiary's care team,
so we reuse `update` on the beneficiary rather than minting a new
permission. Cross-structure assignment is blocked at three layers:
  1. The exists rule scopes the intervenant to the current tenant
  2. BasePolicy::before() denies update on a foreign beneficiary
  3. IntervenantAssignmentService throws 422 if the FKs disagree
AttachIntervenantRequest.title: AttachIntervenantRequest

totp_code.description:
Block A / #55 — optional 6-digit TOTP. Required for users
whose role mandates MFA AND who have already enrolled.
The controller checks both branches; we just validate the
shape here.

user_id.description:
user_id is optional — when absent, the controller registers
the authenticated user (self-service path). RH/coord can
register someone else by passing user_id.

id.description:
Block A / #56 — client-assigned UUID for offline-first mobile.
Optional. When the mobile app creates an incident while
offline it generates a UUID locally; on reconnect it sends
it here so a network retry of the same POST is idempotent.
The service either returns the existing row or creates with
this id.

SubmitQvctResponseRequest.description:
Request body for an anonymous response submission. Authorization is
scoped to the campaign (`respond` ability on QvctCampaignPolicy) — the
service layer enforces the open/closed window separately.

Anonymity reminder: this request never reads $this->user() into the
payload — only into the gate check. The controller passes only the
campaign + answers + optional team_tag to QvctService::recordResponse.

items.description:
Permissive on values — the questionnaire shape lives in
qvct_questionnaires.questions; deep validation against it
is service-layer territory (different question scales etc).

SubmitQvctResponseRequest.title: SubmitQvctResponseRequest

SubscribeStructureRequest.description:
Subscribe / upgrade a structure to a paid tier. Spec:
PHASE2_PROGRESS.md C1.

Authorization: only users with `structure.configure` (dirigeant +
platform admins) can change the structure's billing state. The
intervenant or coordinateur shouldn't be able to enroll the
organisation in a paid plan they didn't authorise.

Stripe payment-method IDs always start with `pm_` — validated via
a starts_with rule plus a length cap to dodge obvious garbage.
SubscribeStructureRequest.title: SubscribeStructureRequest

SyncBatchRequest.description:
Validates a batch of queued mobile operations posted to /api/v1/sync/batch.

Per-operation payload validation lives in SyncBatchService (each `kind`
has its own shape). Here we enforce only the envelope: the array, the
required keys, and a hard cap on batch size to bound memory + work.

The cap (200) matches one offline workday for an intervenant
(≈8 visits × multiple events each). Batches larger than this are
almost always client bugs (corrupt queue) and should be rejected fast
rather than consume a worker.

payload.description:
`present` (not `required`) so an empty `payload: {}` is valid.
Some ops (e.g. intervention.check_in without GPS) carry no fields.

SyncBatchRequest.title: SyncBatchRequest

UpdateBeneficiaryContactsRequest.description:
Strict-scope update — only non-medical contact fields. The dossier
médical (allergies, médical_history, current_treatments) is NEVER
touched by this request: the corresponding rule keys are absent, so
`$request->validated()` would not contain them even if a malicious
client sent them.

Used by BeneficiaryController::updateContacts on /beneficiaries/{id}/contacts.
UpdateBeneficiaryContactsRequest.title: UpdateBeneficiaryContactsRequest
